So if your laptop includes Windows, a year of Office 365, and anti-virus then these things are most likely worked into the price. If you just plan to install Linux then you don't need these things but in that circumstance I'd usually recommend just buying a used laptop. So I'm curious are there manufacturers which will sell you a new laptop with just a blank hard drive and no software?
Where can you buy laptops new without software?
It's offset by massive volume discounts and the usually paid bloatware, so the manufacturer doesn't spend much on the OS.
Some barebones manufacturers like Clevo sell laptops without an OS. You save a bunch of money by buying and putting in your own SSD/memory as well.

Dell sells a "developer" version of their XPS laptops with Ubuntu preinstalled. Saves you $100 off the list price as well. It's pretty simple to install anything else over that.

Also, their XPS models tend to be really nice IIRC, so no worries about old/shitty specs.

Further to this, Dell's new Inspiron (I think) that can come with Ubuntu too can also come without OS. Also without a hard drive at all if you really want.

System76 is another place that specialises in Linux laptops only. Unfortunately it looked to me as though the economies of scale works against them. It seems as though you might pay a premium over a major manufacturer including the Windows tax. (But I see that they've already been mentioned.

Instead of getting a laptop without software, I suggest you find an online store that sells Linux-based laptops. Try to search for one, you might be pleasantly surprised. Plus you know the more exotic hardware (most often the wi-fi) works on the laptop before you download it.

Back in 2012, I ordered a laptop online and requested no operating system be installed on it.

I ended up paying $200 less for it and it came with an empty hard drive.

Chromebooks

They come with Chrome OS, which is based in Linux and isn't part of the price of the laptop. Also, you should give Chrome OS a chance, for day to day basic use, it's the best version of Linux I've ever used. Updates are seamless and never interrupt. It doesn't require antivirus. It always works and is very intuitive. Very fast and crazy long battery life as well.

You can also install Linux on Chromebooks

You can also google for "buy barebones laptop" although a quick search to the usual vendors does not bring up too many common models/brandnames

Even amazon tends to show models with specs like i7 32GB ram, 512 SSD etc. with prices to match

YMMV
xoticpc is where I've purchased a few laptops with out OS. Cleo/Sager give you quite a few options to choose from.
